title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals transform fault in the Zabargad Fracture Zone
summary: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep. The southern cluster’s diffuse seismicity and predominantly left-lateral strike-slip focal mechanisms reveal a NE–SW transform fault, which the authors describe as possibly in an early development stage. The northern cluster instead shows NW–SE normal-faulting lineaments related to extension.
ai_technology: OBSTransformer deep-learning phase picker, transfer-learned from EQTransformer and used through SeisBench
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST); GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research

evidence.tested: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep.
evidence.unknown: The transform fault is inferred from the southern seismicity pattern and selected-event focal mechanisms, not directly imaged along its full geometry; the authors describe it as possibly in an early development stage. The catalog covers a 12-month deployment and is a snapshot that may not capture episodic ridge seismicity. Exact spreading-axis configuration remains uncertain. The earthquake-processing workflow was not fully automatic: investigators manually reviewed and corrected picks, removed events recorded by fewer than three stations, and used manual focal-mechanism analysis.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers compared EQTransformer, OBSTransformer and PickBlue for automatic earthquake detection and P/S phase picking on continuous ocean-bottom and land-station data. OBSTransformer was selected because it detected more events than EQTransformer while yielding fewer false detections than PickBlue and closer agreement with manual picks. The resulting detections and picks were manually checked and corrected, then used in the catalog from which the clusters and focal-mechanism analysis revealed the faulting pattern.
